chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to order his servants that they should not slaughter until the dawn emerges. In the Miscellaneous (Hadith) regarding Friday.
ai.seo_question: When is the best time to slaughter an animal according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the practice of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) in delaying slaughter until after the emergence of dawn, distinguishing it from the general prohibition of slaughtering during specific sun times. It underscores the Shia emphasis on aligning daily economic acts with ritual purity and the prophetic tradition of avoiding times associated with idolatrous practices. This timing ensures the meat is prepared in a state of spiritual readiness, reflecting the broader Islamic principle of integrating worship with mundane activities.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Amro, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Aban Bin Taghlub, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> used to order his<sup>asws</sup> servants that they should not slaughter until the emergence of the dawn’. – In a miscellaneous (Hadeeth) regarding the day of Friday.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Aban ibn Taghlib who has said the following:
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that Ali ibn al-Husayn, would command his servants not to slaughter any animal before dawn on Friday. This Hadith is of rare Ahadith about Fridays.’”
